## Modifications

**File: `src/main/java/com/garbagemule/MobArena/ArenaListener.java`**

In the food level change event handler, the condition for cancelling the event was modified. Previously, when the arena was running and `lockFoodLevel` was enabled, the event was cancelled for **any** player triggering a food level change, regardless of whether they were actually participating in the arena. The fix adds an additional check `arena.inArena(p)` to the condition, ensuring the food level change is only cancelled if the affected player is actually inside the arena.

## Relationship

This is a single-file, single-location fix. The change tightens the scope of the existing food-level-lock logic by adding a guard condition (`arena.inArena(p)`) before the previously existing `lockFoodLevel` check. This prevents the bug where food level changes for players outside the arena (i.e., anyone on the server) were being incorrectly cancelled whenever an arena was running with food level locking enabled. No other files or methods are involved—the fix is isolated to the `onFoodLevelChange`-related logic within `ArenaListener`.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
`if (arena.isRunning()) {`
`if (lockFoodLevel) {`
`event.setCancelled(true);`
Reason: When the arena is running, the code only checks whether `lockFoodLevel` is enabled before cancelling the `FoodLevelChangeEvent`, without checking whether the player `p` who triggered the event is actually inside the arena. Since this listener listens to the server-wide `FoodLevelChangeEvent`, this causes the food level lock to be incorrectly applied to every player on the server, not just those participating in the arena.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
`if (arena.inArena(p) && lockFoodLevel) {`
Reason: Adding the `arena.inArena(p)` check ensures that the event is only cancelled if the player triggering the food level change is actually a participant in the running arena. This properly scopes the food level lock to arena participants, preventing it from affecting players elsewhere on the server.
